headline: Transformation program targeting $2B EBITDA improvement while navigating weak chemical cycle through cost restructuring and feedstock optimization.
standout_number: Q2 2026 operating EBIT of $1.648B with polyethylene driving recovery; $2B+ targeted near-term EBITDA lift from Transform to Outperform program.
whats_different: Rather than waiting out the cycle, Dow is aggressively restructuring the cost base, simplifying operations, and leveraging feedstock flexibility and asset integration to defend downstream franchises through the downturn. The company is explicitly shrinking weaker footprint while preserving higher-return businesses.
watch: Execution of the Transform to Outperform program cost targets and whether polyethylene price recovery can be sustained; chemical cycle timing and whether the company can stabilize margins before competitive pressure returns.

headline: Record free cash flow generation ($7.3B in 2025) enabling large capital returns while simplifying portfolio through divestitures and strengthening balance sheet to net cash position.
standout_number: Full-year 2025 adjusted EBITDA of $13.48B; net cash position of $2.1B at year-end after $3.4B debt reduction and $3.4B shareholder returns.
whats_different: Newmont is converting commodity strength into a more repeatable capital-allocation model rather than an empire-building strategy. The company is actively reshaping itself through portfolio discipline, debt reduction, and formalized repurchase programs while maintaining project development spending.
watch: Whether the capital allocation framework can sustain higher buyback levels without sacrificing balance sheet flexibility; reserve life and project execution quality at key assets like Ahafo North, Lihir, and Cadia.

headline: Juanicipio acquisition transforming the company into a silver-centered platform with $1B+ annual returns framework and record cash balance of $1.8B.
standout_number: Q1 2026 record cash of $1.8B including attributable Juanicipio cash; company targeting up to $1B in returns in 2026 with excess free cash flow directed to buybacks.
whats_different: Pan American is explicitly shifting identity from diversified precious metals to a silver-weighted platform where gold cash generation funds growth and returns. The Juanicipio acquisition is not just a transaction; it is a strategic anchor that raises production profile and lowers all-in sustaining costs.
watch: Juanicipio ramp execution and cost trajectory; silver price environment and whether higher-quality ore reduces per-ounce mining costs as planned; capital deployment at La Colorada Skarn expansion.

headline: International growth driving 10.7% sales growth with EMEA expanding 32.6% and product innovation sustaining 55% gross margins despite tariff and freight pressures.
standout_number: FY2025 net sales of $8.29B up 10.7%; Q4 2025 net sales outside US reached 42% of total; EMEA grew 32.6% in dollars reflecting strong international momentum.
whats_different: Monster succeeds through brand intensity, distribution depth with Coca-Cola partnership, and continuous innovation in adjacent energy categories beyond core energy drink. The business model depends on repeat-use energy habits, identity-driven demand, and retail presence as much as product quality.
watch: Weaker alcohol brands and whether adjacent categories can achieve profitability; international expansion sustainability and regulatory scrutiny on stimulation and ingredients; whether Coca-Cola partnership remains as central.

headline: FY2026 margin recovery through ERP modernization and GOJO integration despite 13% organic sales decline, signaling operational repair over effortless pricing power.
standout_number: Q4 FY2026 organic sales declined 13% and gross margin declined 520 basis points to 41.3%, but management emphasized completing GOJO acquisition and U.S. ERP implementation as transitional investments.
whats_different: Clorox is rebuilding margin through system modernization, portfolio discipline, and AI-enabled innovation acceleration (65% cycle-time reduction) rather than relying on brand pricing. The household-cleaning moat depends on trusted daily-use positioning but requires execution discipline and modern systems.
watch: Whether the Glad bags and wraps joint-venture wind-down impacts revenue; GOJO integration success and margin recovery trajectory; consumer value-seeking behavior and whether cleaning and health-hygiene demand holds firm.

headline: 39 consecutive quarters of top-line growth and productivity-funded reinvestment showing resilient staples model, though FY2026 Q4 organic sales stalled suggesting margin pressure.
standout_number: FY2025 net sales of $84.3B with 39 consecutive quarters of growth; FY2026 Q4 organic sales flat and core EPS grew only 4%, signaling pressure despite strong cash generation of $17.8B operating cash flow.
whats_different: P&G defends its staples position through focused daily-use categories, brand superiority, portfolio breadth, and operational execution rather than consumer trend-chasing. The model is built on productivity-funded reinvestment paired with large dividends and buybacks, not premium positioning.
watch: Tariff impact on margins and whether productivity gains can offset input costs; organic sales stalling in FY2026 Q4 suggests consumer pressure; ability to maintain both reinvestment and shareholder returns if growth slows further.

headline: Brand-centric strategy transitioning from toy manufacturer to IP-driven play and entertainment platform with theatrical releases, digital games, and cross-format engagement.
standout_number: Full-year 2025 net sales of $5,348M down 1%, but Q2 2026 revenue up 10% driven by Hot Wheels (14%), Action Figures (35%) and digital games following Mattel163 acquisition; targeting record openings in 2026.
whats_different: Mattel is not building a pure product business. It is constructing an IP franchise system where toys, films, and digital games reinforce demand loops. This requires higher advertising spend, royalty payments, and capital for infrastructure, but aims at deeper consumer engagement.
watch: Tariff and cost pressures on physical goods profitability; success of digital games strategy and Mattel163 integration; theatrical release performance (Masters of the Universe) and whether movie tie-ins drive toy demand; execution of multi-year IP strategy against Hasbro's cleaner licensing model.

headline: Multi-basin portfolio optimization through asset rotation and market access improvement, with Montney and Permian emphasis plus 10-year gas supply contracts to improve realizations.
standout_number: 2025 production of 224.3 MMBOE with U.S. Permian producing 51.9 MMbbl oil at $9.95/BOE vs Canadian operations at $13.43/BOE; company using forward gas contracts at Chicago/JKM pricing plus longer-term transport agreements to improve economics.
whats_different: Ovintiv is distinct because it monetizes basin exposure through commercial structure and route access, not only drilling activity. The company explicitly uses firm transport contracts, downstream pricing optionality, and asset rotation to improve realized economics across North American oil, gas, and NGL production.
watch: Success of Montney and Permian acquisitions in delivering returns; condensate and NGL price environment affecting realization margins; effectiveness of forward gas contracts and downstream market access in insulating from basin pricing weakness.

headline: Integrated NGL, gas processing, and export infrastructure platform targeting $3B net growth projects while maintaining record pipelines and facilities volumes of 3.7 MMboe/d.
standout_number: Full-year 2025 adjusted EBITDA of C$4.289B; Q2 2026 sanctioned C$3B in growth projects including Greenlight Electricity Centre and Heartland Extraction Plant; record annual Pipelines and Facilities volumes of 3.7 MMboe/d.
whats_different: Pembina is more than a crude-takeaway operator. The company is an integrated corridor system monetizing gas processing, NGL fractionation, extraction, power generation, and export logistics through interconnected facilities and long-term customer contracts. Growth comes from volume and installed-base expansion rather than tariff rate optimization alone.
watch: Execution of C$425M+ expansion projects and Greenlight/Heartland sanction; Cedar LNG remarketing progress; whether integrated customer projects like Tourmaline/PGI agreements and Redwater Complex fractionation continue attracting capital investment.

headline: AUM reached $15.3T in Q2 2026 with record first-half flows of $321B, driven by ETF scale, private markets expansion (HPS $165B AUM lift), and technology-service revenue reaching $1.981B annually.
standout_number: Q2 2026 revenue of $6.352B with adjusted operating margin of 45.9%; full-year 2025 AUM of $14.0T with record net inflows of $698B; technology services and subscription revenue of $1.981B in FY2025.
whats_different: BlackRock is not only monetizing market beta or indexed scale. The company is building a financial platform that monetizes ETF distribution, private markets, technology services, data, and outsourcing inside one operating model. The margin profile reflects pricing power across multiple monetization layers.
watch: HPS and Preqin integration success and whether acquisitions deliver promised synergies; private-markets adoption trends and fee compression dynamics; ETF competitive intensity and whether BlackRock maintains pricing power as alternatives grow.

headline: 10% full-year revenue growth with 6% underlying revenue growth in 2Q26, showing consistent demand for risk placement and advisory services with light balance-sheet burden.
standout_number: Full-year 2025 revenue of $27.0B up 10% with adjusted EPS of $9.75; 2Q26 GAAP EPS of $2.63 with adjusted EPS of $2.96 and 5% underlying revenue growth, reflecting steady demand for advice and market access.
whats_different: Marsh monetizes institutional anxiety, regulation, and complexity through workflow ownership and repeated client placement rather than through asset risk warehousing. The business is less capital-intensive than banking or mortgage REITs and depends on trust, expertise, and client dependence.
watch: Greensill litigation resolution and whether one-time charges recur; competitive intensity in insurance brokerage and consulting fees; economic sensitivity of insurance placements to corporate capex and M&A cycles.

headline: Thrift-to-business-bank repositioning with return on tangible common equity reaching 11% in Q3 FY2026, showing successful transition from mortgage lending toward business solutions.
standout_number: Q3 FY2026 net income of $66.1M with diluted EPS of $0.84; return on tangible common equity of 11.0%; net interest margin holding at 2.81% as deposit mix improves with transaction deposits rising and time deposits declining.
whats_different: WaFd is not a frozen thrift institution. Management is explicitly repositioning the company from mortgage lending toward business banking, using a deposit franchise and branch system as advantages while improving deposit mix and customer relationship depth.
watch: Success of business banking strategy and whether loan demand strengthens faster than projected; credit quality and whether non-performing assets remain elevated; deposit margin sustainability as funding costs normalize; competitive intensity for business relationships in western regional markets.

headline: Home-based institutional supply platform serving 4.3M patients annually, scaling through capitated partnerships and digital tools ($512K myAPP users up 56%) while divesting Diabetes Health.
standout_number: Q2 2026 net revenue of $740.3M up 12.7% with organic growth of 15.9%; company selling Diabetes Health for $235M and joint-ventured eCommerce asset to launch integrated sleep retail platform.
whats_different: AdaptHealth does not sell consumer products. It monetizes recurring equipment and supply access, referral relationships, payer routing, and home-based care continuity. The business depends on acute-care hospitals, sleep labs, skilled nursing, payors, and field execution—not on direct consumer demand.
watch: Capitated partnership rollout complexity and margin impact; unexpected manufacturer price increases and their effect on profitability; successful Diabetes Health divestiture execution; whether myAPP digital adoption translates to improved retention and margin quality.

headline: Installed base of 11,100+ da Vinci systems and 995 Ion systems growing procedure volumes 16-17% while instruments-and-accessories revenue grows 23%, proving platform stickiness.
standout_number: Q2 2026 revenue of $2.89B; worldwide procedures grew approximately 17% including da Vinci procedures up 16% and Ion procedures up 39%; instruments and accessories revenue rose 23%, showing strong platform leverage.
whats_different: Intuitive monetizes not single device sales but installed-base economics: system placements drive recurring procedure growth, which drives instruments-and-accessories demand, which drives service revenue and utilization deepening. The moat is workflow embedment, not product novelty.
watch: Ion procedure adoption trajectory and whether it can accelerate meaningful contribution; international expansion opportunity and market penetration in existing geographies; da Vinci 5 adoption and whether new platform features justify customer trade-up spending.

headline: Separation into Honeywell Technologies (pure automation) on 2026-06-29 positions company as AI-driven industrial controls platform serving data centers, utilities, and building automation.
standout_number: Q2 2026 post-spin Honeywell Technologies sales of $5.187B with segment margin of 19.0%; Q2 consolidated revenue was $9.719B; backlog rose to $38.3B reflecting strong AI and data-center infrastructure demand.
whats_different: Honeywell Technologies is not an aerospace vendor after separation. It is an automation, controls, and AI-infrastructure modernization platform where building systems, process automation, data-center infrastructure, and fire safety converge. Growth depends on installed-base leverage and AI-driven digitization.
watch: Honeywell Aerospace spin-off performance and separation-cost realization; Quantinuum deconsolidation impact and quantum-computing investment strategy; backlog conversion quality and whether data-center and AI demand can sustain guidance; margin expansion execution in standalone company.

headline: Federal mission contractor with backlog of $16.8B planning 2027 spin-off of Mission Technology Solutions, creating pure-play federal-tech and commercial-infrastructure companies.
standout_number: Full-year 2025 revenue of $7.786B with 64% from federal defense/intel and federal civilian clients; Mission Technology Solutions planned spin targeting January 2027; backlog grew to $16.8B with options reaching $6.3B.
whats_different: KBR is not a generic construction name. It monetizes program complexity, federal mission criticality, defense readiness, and long-cycle client dependence through cost-reimbursable and time-and-materials contracts. The planned MTS spin-off reflects belief that federal and commercial economics deserve separate platforms.
watch: MTS spin-off execution timing and stranded-cost exposure; federal budget environment for defense and civilian agencies; commercial and industrial capex trends affecting STS backlog; contract mix and whether fixed-price work becomes more common or remains manageable.

headline: AI infrastructure power and thermal provider with 2.9x Q4 book-to-bill, Q2 2026 backlog of $15B (up 109%), and record organic orders of 252% YoY in Q4 2025.
standout_number: Q2 2026 net sales of $3,274M up 18% organically; adjusted operating margin of 22.6%; full-year backlog of $15.0B up 109% year-over-year; Q4 2025 organic orders grew 252% with book-to-bill of 2.9x.
whats_different: Vertiv is converting AI infrastructure demand into both growth and balance-sheet strength by selling power, cooling, and thermal infrastructure to hyperscale and colocation customers. This is not adjacent to AI; it is fundamental to AI deployment feasibility.
watch: Backlog conversion pace and whether delivery schedules can keep up with demand; supply-chain constraints in power and thermal components; margin sustainability as competitive intensity rises; leverage and refinancing needs if acquisition activity continues.

headline: Largest U.S. homebuilder by volume targeting 83,800-84,300 closings in FY2026 with $370K average closing price and elevated incentives reflecting affordability constraints.
standout_number: Q3 FY2026 homes closed of 23,983 (up 4%) at average closing price of $370.4K; full-year FY2025 net income of $3.6B on revenue of $34.3B; company targeting FY2026 closings at 83,800-84,300 range (down from FY2025 guidance).
whats_different: D.R. Horton succeeds through geographic scale (126 markets, 36 states), integrated financing and lot control (via Forestar), local operator autonomy, and disciplined capital allocation rather than broad pricing power. The builder is defending returns through incentives and execution rather than price appreciation.
watch: First-time buyer affordability and incentive levels required to sustain demand; mortgage rate environment and whether rate cuts stimulate traffic; lot acquisition pace and Forestar performance; whether the company can maintain 12-13% pre-tax profit margins with current closings guidance.

headline: Data-center and industrial reshoring driving environmental infrastructure demand with Q2 2026 orders of $798.5M (up 191%) post-Thermon acquisition and backlog of $1.8B.
standout_number: Q2 2026 orders of $798.5M up 191%; backlog of $1.8B up 164%; company raised full-year 2026 guidance to revenue of $1.30B-$1.375B and adjusted EBITDA of $200M-$225M after Thermon integration ahead of synergy targets.
whats_different: CECO monetizes environmental and process-control infrastructure across air, water, and thermal management for data centers, semiconductors, utilities, and reshored manufacturing. The company benefits when AI and industrial demand pull in older environmental-control categories.
watch: Thermon integration success and synergy realization; project execution and backlog conversion as free cash flow turned negative in Q1 2026; margin sustainability as competitive intensity increases; data-center customer concentration and whether diversity improves.

headline: Global tower owner (149K sites) plus CoreSite datacenters monetizing mobile-data growth and AI cloud demand, though DISH default and churn disrupted 2026 reported billings growth.
standout_number: Q2 2026 AFFO attributable to common shareholders of $1.264B up 3.8%; global tower portfolio plus 30 data-center facilities; DISH churn of ~5% of tenant billings beginning Jan 1 2026 due to Strategic Collocation Agreement default.
whats_different: American Tower is not only a tower landlord. It monetizes both wireless-network edge (towers) and enterprise-cloud interconnection (CoreSite), making it a platform where bandwidth demand, cloud adoption, and AI scaling all support recurring lease economics.
watch: DISH dispute resolution and whether churn stabilizes; organic tenant billings growth recovery once DISH comparisons normalize; CoreSite growth acceleration and whether data-center expansion justifies capex; international FX and AT&T Mexico arbitration exposure.

headline: Off-price value retailer posting FY2025 sales of $22.8B (up 8%) with 5% comp growth driven by customer traffic, compelling bargains, and disciplined inventory management.
standout_number: FY2025 sales of $22.8B up 8% with net income of $2.1B and EPS of $6.61; Q1 2026 sales increased 21% with comp growth of 17% and operating margin of 13.4% due to strong traffic and merchandise leverage.
whats_different: Ross succeeds through off-price value positioning and branded-bargain sourcing rather than brand ownership or ecosystem scale. The moat is execution: merchandise assortment quality, customer engagement through marketing, and inventory discipline in capturing closeout availability.
watch: Tariff impact on sourcing costs and whether the off-price model can absorb tariffs better than traditional retail; brand-name supplier availability and closeout inventory as other retailers reduce excess; customer traffic sustainability in more stable consumer environment.

headline: FY2025 core merchandise challenged (sales down 1.7%) but non-merchandise layer strengthening with Target Circle 360 membership, Roundel advertising, and same-day delivery all growing 25%+.
standout_number: FY2025 net sales of $104.8B down 1.7% but non-merchandise sales grew over 25%; Q1 2026 net sales increased 6.7% to $25.4B with comparable digital sales up 8.9% and non-merchandise growth of 24.6%.
whats_different: Target is building a second monetization layer on top of struggling core merchandise. Target Circle 360 membership, Roundel advertising, Target+, and same-day delivery fulfillment are expanding the model from product retailer toward convenience, advertising, and marketplace platform.
watch: Core merchandise stabilization and whether traffic recovery is durable; Target Circle 360 adoption and economics; Roundel advertising growth and customer acceptance; capex intensity of same-day and supply-chain modernization versus profitability improvement.

headline: Asset-light lodging franchisor growing system-wide rooms 4% with record development pipeline of 261K rooms and mid-30% FeePAR premium to existing systems.
standout_number: Full-year 2025 diluted EPS of $2.50 (down 31% on impairments) but adjusted diluted EPS of $4.58 up 6%; system-wide rooms grew 4%; development pipeline reached record 259K rooms with 30% FeePAR premium.
Full-year 2025 adjusted EPS of $4.58 up 6%; Q2 2026 U.S. RevPAR growth of 2%; system-wide rooms grew 4%; development pipeline reached record ~261K rooms with 30% FeePAR premium to existing systems.
whats_different: Wyndham monetizes everyday domestic travel and value-conscious lodging through franchise relationships rather than owned assets. The model depends on franchisee demand, room growth, ancillary revenue expansion, and capital return—not on premium occupancy or rate recovery.
watch: U.S. RevPAR recovery trajectory and whether momentum can sustain; Revo-related fee deferrals and their timing of resolution; development pace and whether higher-FeePAR openings can offset lower RevPAR on mature base; international softness and China exposure.

headline: Integrated Asia-focused resort operator with Marina Bay Sands and Macao portfolio generating significant cash despite gaming mix and hold volatility affecting reported results.
standout_number: Q2 2026 net revenue of $3.15B with consolidated adjusted property EBITDA of $1.12B; full-year 2025 net income of $1.63B ($2.35 per share); unrestricted cash of $3.38B with $4.26B additional revolving facility availability.
whats_different: Sands monetizes luxury-integrated-resort economics in scarce Asian destinations where hotels, gaming, retail, conventions, and entertainment reinforce the same tourist wallet. The moat is iconic property control and tourism infrastructure position, not gaming efficiency.
watch: Marina Bay Sands expansion capex and return realization; Macao gaming mix and policy environment affecting volumes; international tourism recovery and China travel demand trends; hold volatility and whether fundamentals improve when normalized; concession renewal risk.

headline: Global travel-booking platform with $26.9B FY2025 revenue, merchant mix rising to 73% of bookings, and $1.9B ARR reach showing shift toward direct consumer and cross-vertical transactions.
standout_number: FY2025 revenue of $26.9B with merchant gross bookings growing to 73% of total mix; flight gross bookings increased 29%; Q2 2026 merchant mix rose to 73% from 69% year-over-year.
whats_different: Booking is not a travel company; it is a distribution and transaction orchestration platform. The economics depend on merchant mix, direct consumer behavior, mobile-app usage, loyalty participation, payment attachment, and cross-vertical transaction volume rather than on supply inventory alone.
watch: Middle East geopolitical impact on international travel demand and fuel costs; merchant mix stabilization at higher levels and whether agency conversions continue; Connected Trip monetization and whether ancillary attach improves margins; international exposure to FX and travel policy shifts.

headline: Connected operations platform reaching $1.991B ARR in Q1 FY2027 with $432M net new ARR in FY2026, powered by labor-capacity constraints and operational AI demand in physical industries.
standout_number: Q1 FY2027 ARR of $1.991B; full-year FY2026 ended Jan 31 with revenue of $1.619B and non-GAAP operating margin of 17%; company frames next growth layer around Operational AI agents automating work and unlocking worker capacity.
whats_different: Samsara is not digital-office software. It is a control layer for physical operations—fleets, equipment, sites, frontline workers—monetizing data collection, workflow visibility, and now AI-driven automation. The moat depends on customer operational ROI and labor-productivity proof rather than feature adoption.
watch: Operational AI and agent adoption pace and whether customers can prove measurable productivity gains; customer concentration and whether vertical expansion reduces dependence on large transportation/logistics base; competitive intensity from enterprise-software incumbents and point-solution vendors.

headline: Enterprise frontline computing platform (rugged devices, RFID, printing, machine vision) with Connected Frontline and Asset Visibility segments showing 15-20% operating margin expansion.
standout_number: FY2025 revenue of $5.396B with operating income of $700M; Q2 2026 revenue of $1.557B with diluted EPS of $4.85; Connected Frontline generated $2.960B FY2025 revenue with operating income of $585M.
whats_different: Zebra monetizes the operational dependence of distributed enterprises on physical-device fleets, workflow software, and asset visibility. The moat is installed-base standardization, enterprise workflow integration, and the switching costs of changing frontline infrastructure.
watch: Elo and Photoneo acquisition synergies and integration success; automation and asset-visibility adoption by enterprise customers; supply-chain normalization and whether margin expansion persists; competitive pressure from hyperscalers and enterprise-software vendors entering edge-hardware categories.

headline: Post-Juniper acquisition (July 2025) AI-era infrastructure platform combining servers, storage, networking, and financing; Q2 FY2026 networking revenue of $2.7B (up 148%) shows transformation progress.
standout_number: Q2 FY2026 revenue of $10.7B up 40% YoY with networking revenue of $2.7B up 148%; Cloud & AI revenue of $7.7B up 22.9%; full-year 2025 adjusted EBITDA likely ~$4B+ reflecting operating leverage.
whats_different: HPE is not a legacy server vendor. It is an enterprise-infrastructure modernization platform combining compute, storage, networking, and AI-upgrade capability. The burden stack is real, but so is the profit pool when enterprises consolidate infrastructure spend around unified systems.
watch: Juniper synergy realization and whether faster-than-planned integration can sustain; gross-margin sustainability as mix shifts and competitive intensity rises; backlog ($38B+) conversion pace and supply-chain constraints; leverage and refinancing needs if growth rate slows.

headline: Edge-network and application-security platform reaching $2.7B RPO in Q2 2026 (up 35% current growth) with 45%+ Fortune 500 customers; positioned for agentic AI and machine-to-machine traffic monetization.
standout_number: Q2 2026 revenue of $696.1M; RPO of $2.7320B up 35% current-year growth; FY2025 revenue of $2.1679B with 74.5% gross margin; 45%+ of Fortune 500 as paying customers.
whats_different: Cloudflare monetizes the control layer where performance, security, and developer tooling converge for application delivery—not pure connectivity or pure security. The platform value increases if machine traffic, APIs, and agentic interaction all flow through the same control point.
watch: GAAP profitability inflection and whether restructuring charges resolve; category convergence and competitive pressure from hyperscalers and security incumbents; customer concentration among large deals and whether net retention rate sustains at high levels; RPO conversion quality.

headline: Programmable edge and application-delivery control platform showing mix shift toward security ($41.7M in Q2 2026, up from $35.4M in Q4 2025) while maintaining 65%+ gross margins.
standout_number: Q2 2026 revenue of $183.3M up 23% with GAAP gross margin of 63.3%; RPO of $341M up 38%; top-ten customer concentration of 37%; LTM net retention rate of 117%.
whats_different: Fastly sits between older CDN incumbents and newer cloud-security platforms. The company monetizes programmable edge control and application-protection intelligence for AI traffic, e-commerce security, and developer deployment—narrower than Cloudflare, broader than pure delivery.
watch: Top-ten customer concentration and whether customer diversification improves; network-services revenue stability as usage-based model faces competition; security revenue growth acceleration and whether it can offset flatter delivery revenue; free cash flow quality and capital intensity.
